The print covers every part of the shirt from the ribbed collar band to the hem and out to both sleeve hems, and wraps around the side seams to the back. Every panel of the shirt, front, shoulders and sleeves, is a panel of the outfit, showing a tweed jacket with chalk-dusted elbow patches. Turn the shirt around and the back carries the matching back of the outfit, printed edge to edge with nothing left plain. One continuous print of the outfit's cloth covers the shirt from collar band to hem and out to both sleeve hems. The shirt is a standard T-shirt shape with a straight hem across the bottom. The printed top garment continues down the shirt to its straight hem, with at most a belt or sash at the waist. The outfit's cloth runs unbroken from the collar band across both shoulders and down both sleeves to their hems, so every part of the shirt is outfit cloth. The uniform fills the whole straight-sided shirt shape edge to edge, the same width at chest, waist and hem. The shirt's sleeves are tailored to end at the elbow, exactly where the outfit's sleeves end. The shirt is solid opaque cotton and every texture and sheen is a printed picture. The picture is only the garment, its cloth, seams, buttons and trims laid flat across the whole shirt like a sewing pattern. It also shows printed cuffs where the sleeves end. It is a trompe-l'oeil T-shirt, a plain cotton shirt pretending to be the outfit. To read as a costume rather than a plain top, it adds the lower garment's colours and pattern as a band across the hem, the collar, neckwear and fastenings of the outfit and the footwear's trim colours as stripes on the cuffs and hem, bold and large enough to identify the outfit from across a room. Any printed skin, such as hands, wrists, neck, chest or forearms, is in a flat printed light tan skin tone.

The shirt's neckline is the outfit's collar opening, the shirt's sleeves carry the outfit's sleeves, and the shirt's hem is the outfit's lower edge, showing a tentacled coat. The back of the shirt is printed just as completely, edge to edge, with the back of the same outfit, its back collar, shoulder blades and the backs of both sleeves. One continuous print of the outfit's cloth covers the shirt from collar band to hem and out to both sleeve hems. The shirt is a standard T-shirt shape with a straight hem across the bottom. The printed top garment continues down the shirt to its straight hem, with at most a belt or sash at the waist. The outfit's cloth runs unbroken from the collar band across both shoulders and down both sleeves to their hems, so every part of the shirt is outfit cloth. The outfit is laid out on the shirt's own rectangle shape, fully covering it from side seam to side seam. The shirt is a long-sleeved T-shirt matching the outfit's long sleeves, printed with the sleeves and cuffs all the way down to the wrist hems. All textures, transparencies and sheens are printed patterns on solid cotton. The picture is only the garment, its cloth, seams, buttons and trims laid flat across the whole shirt like a sewing pattern. It also shows printed cuffs at the sleeve hems. The print wraps around the sides so the outfit seems to continue around the body. The tee is clearly a costume tee, not a plain shirt, it shows the held item or gear of the outfit, shown as a patch or large motif on the chest or a sleeve, its pockets, flaps and trims and the headwear's emblem or crest worked into the chest, so anyone can tell at a glance what outfit it stands for. Any printed skin, such as hands, wrists, neck, chest or forearms, is in a flat printed light tan skin tone.

The printed outfit runs from the neckline to the hem and from one sleeve hem to the other, its shoulders on the shirt's shoulder seams, showing a black coat with a prayer shawl. The print wraps all the way round, the back of the shirt shows the rear of the outfit from the back collar to the hem and along both sleeves. One continuous print of the outfit's cloth covers the shirt from collar band to hem and out to both sleeve hems. It is an ordinary T-shirt in shape, with a straight open hem and sleeves cut to match the outfit's sleeves. Only the upper garment is printed, running all the way down to the shirt's straight hem. The outfit's cloth runs unbroken from the collar band across both shoulders and down both sleeves to their hems, so every part of the shirt is outfit cloth. The uniform fills the whole straight-sided shirt shape edge to edge, the same width at chest, waist and hem. A long-sleeved shirt is used so the outfit's long sleeves fit exactly, printed full length to the shirt's wrist hems. The shirt is solid opaque cotton and every texture and sheen is a printed picture. The picture is only the garment, its cloth, seams, buttons and trims laid flat across the whole shirt like a sewing pattern. It also shows a printed collar continuing the outfit up to the neckline and printed cuffs and wrists at the sleeve hems. It is the kind of novelty tee that tricks the eye from across a room. To read as a costume rather than a plain top, it adds the collar, neckwear and fastenings of the outfit, the held item or gear of the outfit, shown as a patch or large motif on the chest or a sleeve and the outfit's badges, insignia and emblems, bold and large enough to identify the outfit from across a room. Any printed skin, such as hands, wrists, neck, chest or forearms, is in a flat printed light tan skin tone.

The outfit is printed across the whole front, over the shoulders and down both sleeves, showing a padded suit with armour pads. Front and back are both fully printed, the back showing how the same outfit looks from behind. The outfit's own cloth covers the whole shirt as one continuous print, so shoulders, sleeves and body are all in the outfit's colours. The shirt keeps the outline of an ordinary T-shirt, round neckline, straight side seams, sleeves, and a straight open hem. The printed top garment continues down the shirt to its straight hem, with at most a belt or sash at the waist. The outfit's collar meets the real collar band, its shoulders sit on the real shoulder seams and its sleeves fill the real sleeves, all in one piece of printed cloth. The outfit is laid out on the shirt's own rectangle shape, fully covering it from side seam to side seam. A long-sleeved shirt is used so the outfit's long sleeves fit exactly, printed full length to the shirt's wrist hems. The shirt is solid opaque cotton and every texture and sheen is a printed picture. Only the outfit's fabric, trims and fastenings are pictured, spread across the entire shirt as a continuous pattern. It also shows printed cuffs where the sleeves end. It is a flat print, not a framed picture, not a small centred graphic, not a standing figure and not a drawing of a garment on a hanger. It carries enough of the costume to be unmistakable, the collar, neckwear and fastenings of the outfit, the footwear's trim colours as stripes on the cuffs and hem and the lower garment's colours and pattern as a band across the hem, all in the outfit's own colours. Any printed skin, such as hands, wrists, neck, chest or forearms, is in a flat printed light tan skin tone.

The picture is only the garment, its cloth, seams, buttons and trims laid flat across the whole shirt like a sewing pattern. It also shows printed cuffs and wrists at the sleeve hems. It is a flat print, not a framed picture, not a small centred graphic, not a standing figure and not a drawing of a garment on a hanger. It carries enough of the costume to be unmistakable, the outfit's badges, insignia and emblems, the headwear's emblem or crest worked into the chest and the footwear's trim colours as stripes on the cuffs and hem, all in the outfit's own colours. Any printed skin, such as hands, wrists, neck, chest or forearms, is in a flat printed light tan skin tone.
